fixtures: Files are copied into the run's data/ folder. There is no git in the sandbox, so the change under review is given as a patch. Line numbers are new-file line numbers.

evals.name: planted-defects
evals.prompt: Can you review data/orders-api.patch before I merge it? It adds the orders repo and handlers and points config at the refunds service.
evals.expected_output: Findings grouped by file, critical first, each with file, new-file line and severity (critical / warning / nit). Critical: SQL injection in src/orders/repo.ts findOrdersByStatus (status concatenated into the SQL, lines 13-15, reachable from the status query parameter); a live refunds API key hard-coded in src/config.ts line 9. Warning or critical: the swallowed error in cancelOrder (repo.ts lines 33-35) that returns true even when the update or refund failed; the off-by-one loop in exportOrders (handler.ts line 14) that skips the first order and reads past the end; the unvalidated, uncapped ids query parameter in exportOrders (handler.ts line 11) that is not limited to the requesting customer's orders. Line numbers are new-file lines from the hunk headers (config.ts line 9, not patch line 93; handler.ts line 14, not patch line 70). Not defects: the generated $1..$n placeholders in findOrdersByIds, and the catch in cancel that rethrows with context. The verdict, request changes, is the last thing in the review.
assertions: Flags SQL injection in findOrdersByStatus (src/orders/repo.ts, status concatenated into the query) as critical
Flags the hard-coded refunds API key in src/config.ts as critical, with the fix of reading it from the environment or a secrets manager
Flags the empty catch in cancelOrder (src/orders/repo.ts) as a swallowed error, at warning or critical, noting it reports success even when the cancel or refund failed
Flags the loop in exportOrders (src/orders/handler.ts) as off by one: it starts at 1 and runs to i <= orders.length, skipping the first order and reading past the end, at warning or critical
Flags that exportOrders takes ids from the query string without validating or capping them, or without restricting them to the requesting customer
Line references are new-file line numbers, not lines of the patch file: the API key is cited at src/config.ts line 9 (not 93) and the export loop at src/orders/handler.ts line 14 (not 70)
Does not report findOrdersByIds (the generated $1, $2 placeholders with ids passed as parameters) as SQL injection
Does not report the catch in the cancel handler, which rethrows with context, as a swallowed error
Findings are grouped under their files, and within each file critical findings come before warnings and nits
The review closes with the verdict, request changes, as its final statement (not only stated up front)

evals.name: refactor-changes-behavior
evals.prompt: Review data/retry-refactor.patch? It's a pure refactor, the PR description is data/retry-refactor-pr.md.
evals.expected_output: The PR claims no behaviour change, but the diff changes behaviour in three ways it does not mention: Capture and Refund now make up to 5 attempts instead of 3; the fixed 200 ms sleep becomes a doubling backoff (and now respects ctx cancellation); and Void, which never retried, now retries. Each unannounced behaviour change is a finding at warning level (more retries on Refund and a newly retried Void also widen the window for duplicate side effects if the provider does not deduplicate). Fix: keep 3 attempts and leave Void alone in this PR, or say in the description that behaviour changes and why. Refund being retried at all without an idempotency key is pre-existing and listed separately, not counted toward the verdict. Findings cite new-file lines (client.go lines around 38-56, retry.go 10-25). Verdict, last: request changes.
assertions: Says the change is not the pure refactor it claims, because it changes behaviour
Flags the attempt count going from 3 to 5 for Capture and Refund
Flags that Void did not retry before and now does
Rates the unannounced behaviour changes as warning (or critical), not as nits or questions
Does not approve as-is: the verdict is request changes, or needs discussion, given as the review's final statement

evals.name: clean-rename
evals.prompt: Review data/late-fee.patch please, it's just renames and a named constant.
evals.expected_output: No critical or warning findings: the change only renames parameters, extracts graceDays and adds doc comments; behaviour is unchanged and the test is updated to match. Naming or comment suggestions, if any, are nits that do not block. Overall: approve.
assertions: Reports no critical findings
Reports no warning findings
Recognises that behaviour is unchanged (same threshold of 30 days, same 2% fee)
Does not claim the tests are missing or need to change behaviour
The overall assessment is approve
